land.text: the colony of British Honduras: 'It became a British colony in 1840, and a Crown colony in 1862'; 'On 1 June 1973, British Honduras was officially renamed Belize'

predecessors.note: The colony has its own dossier (british-honduras, 1783-1981), which dissolves into this state on 21 September 1981. Cliopatria has no colony row; its Belize row begins in 1983 and its British Colonial Empire aggregate still touches Belize 1983-1995.

capitals.name: Belmopan
capitals.note: After Hurricane Hattie (1961) the page says the damage 'prompted the relocation of the capital some 80 kilometres (50 mi) inland to the planned city of Belmopan'. It gives no date for the move, which precedes the dossier's start (the british-honduras dossier cites the British Honduras page for 1971, 'Belize City (1862-1971); Belmopan (1971-1981)'). Coordinates are the gazetteer's Natural Earth point.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Belize row begins in 1983, two years after independence (21 September 1981); the colony of British Honduras has no Cliopatria row. The country outline is used (84 grid cells, about 21,244 km2).

correction.text: Belize: 'It has an area of 22,970 square kilometres' (infobox 22,966 km2)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 34-vertex polygon is 22,878.8 km2 against the infobox 22,966 km2 (ratio 1.00); its bbox is -89.17..-88.03, 15.91..18.48. On the 253 km2 grid the polygon resolves to 75 cells (about 18,968 km2) against 84 for Natural Earth's outline (about 21,244 km2), 10 cells fewer and one (-88.63, 16.27) outside it; the correction names the country. Same land through 2023; the page records no border change since independence.

region.text: Belize, the former colony of British Honduras, independent of the United Kingdom

ledger.note: 21 September 1981: Belize becomes independent of the United Kingdom. 'Belize achieved its independence from the United Kingdom on 21 September 1981.' The History of Belize page adds: 'Independence came to Belize on 21 September 1981 after the Belize Act 1981, without reaching an agreement with Guatemala.' After independence 'about 1,500 British troops remained in Belize to deter any possible Guatemalan incursions' and 'British soldiers were withdrawn in 1994'; that garrison stayed 'to deter any possible Guatemalan incursions', is not an occupation of another state's land and moves no border.

wars.name: Guatemalan claim to Belize (no war)
wars.outcome: No fighting over ground and no change of border. Guatemala refused to ratify the 1981 Heads of Agreement and independence came 'without reaching an agreement with Guatemala' (History of Belize). 'Guatemala recognised Belize's independence in 1991' (dispute page; the History of Belize page says 1992); a 'Special Agreement' on submitting the issue to the ICJ 'was signed on 8 December 2008'; Guatemala's referendum of 15 April 2018 and Belize's of 8 May 2019 approved the referral, and the case was still before the ICJ at the dossier's end (written phase closed June 2023). The claim 'amounts to 12,272 km2 ... or roughly 53% of Belizean territory', from the Sibun River to the Sarstoon; Guatemala 'has never occupied any part of Belize'.
wars.note: The Belize page says 'Throughout Belize's history, Guatemala has claimed sovereignty over all or part of Belizean territory' and, for the 1960s-70s, the History page says 'Guatemala had repeatedly threatened to use force to take over British Honduras'. The two pages disagree on the year of recognition (Belize page: three years before the 1994 troop withdrawal, i.e. 1991; History page: 1992). The dedicated dispute article would not load. Because no campaign took or held ground there is no contest_start; the claimed land is not drawn as contested. Reviewer am-08-l (2026-10-24): the dedicated article loads under the title 'Belizean–Guatemalan territorial dispute' (the guatemala and british-honduras dossiers cite it); the end year was moved from 2008 to 2024 because the claim is unsettled and pending at the ICJ (guatemala's war entry runs 1859-2024), and the 1991 recognition, the 2008 Special Agreement and the 2018 and 2019 referendums are taken from it. It also lists armed incidents without any change of ground (February 2000, 20 April 2016, April 2019 on the Sarstoon), so no contest zone is drawn.

certainty.note: 'the Hondo and the Sarstoon River, delineate much of the country's northern and southern boundaries' (Belize page); the Anglo-Guatemalan Treaty of 1859 'set the present-day western boundary' (History of Belize), but Guatemala claims 'all or part' of the territory, so the Guatemalan frontier is a surveyed line that is not accepted by both sides.

sources.note: Added by reviewer am-08-l: recognition 'in 1991', Special Agreement 8 December 2008, referendums 15 April 2018 (Guatemala) and 8 May 2019 (Belize), ICJ case pending, claim of 12,272 km2 from the Sibun to the Sarstoon, 'never occupied any part of Belize'.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Belize, History of Belize). Four URLs for the territorial-dispute article returned 'url_not_found' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belize%E2%80%93Guatemala_territorial_dispute, the same with a literal en dash, with a hyphen, and the titles Guatemala-Belize and Guatemalan-Belizean territorial dispute); History of Belize was opened instead and the dispute is recorded only as far as that page and the Belize page go. Start year: independence 21 September 1981; Cliopatria's Belize row begins in 1983, so a 1981-1982 keyframe is added. The colony is the separate dossier british-honduras (type colony, 1783-1981, successor belize). Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row still touches Belize until 1995 (seed neighbours 1983-1995), so eu-11 should release the land in 1981. Cliopatria's polygon is 10 grid cells short of Natural Earth's outline (its east edge is -88.03 against -87.84 for Natural Earth's cells), hence adjust verdicts naming the country. Disagreements: the year Guatemala recognised Belize (Belize page implies 1991, History page says 1992); the date of the move to Belmopan is on neither page (the british-honduras dossier gives 1971 from its own page). The Mexican boundary (Hondo River) and the Sarstoon River boundary are not dated on the pages opened. Considered and left out: the 1859 treaty (before the dossier), the 1862 and 1973 colony events (belong to british-honduras), the 1964 self-government. Guatemala (am-08) and Mexico (am-08) are the land neighbours; no event gives or takes land from either. No ruler list: a Commonwealth realm whose head of state is the British monarch. Reviewer am-08-l (2026-10-24): the dispute article does exist, at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belizean%E2%80%93Guatemalan_territorial_dispute; the war entry now runs to 2024 and cites it (it gives 1991 for Guatemala's recognition, agreeing with the Belize page).
